quickSummary: An inflorescence is a floral cluster on a peduncle. Racemose inflorescences have indeterminate growth with acropetal/centripetal flower maturation. Cymose inflorescences terminate in a flower with determinate basipetal/centrifugal maturation. Special types include Cyathium (Euphorbia), Verticillaster (Ocimum), and Hypanthodium (Ficus).

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Racemose = Acropetal + Centripetal (Indeterminate); Cymose = Basipetal + Centrifugal (Determinate). Cyathium has 1 female flower surrounded by single-stamen male flowers.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
INFLORESCENCE ARCHITECTURE
                                     │
         ┌───────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────┐
         ▼                           ▼                           ▼
   RACEMOSE TYPES               CYMOSE TYPES              SPECIAL TYPES
 (Indeterminate Growth)       (Determinate Growth)       (Highly Condensed)
 ├── Main Axis Grows Continuously├── Axis Ends in Flower   ├── Cyathium (Euphorbia)
 ├── Centripetal Opening      ├── Centrifugal Opening    ├── Verticillaster (Ocimum)
 └── Acropetal Sequence       └── Basipetal Sequence     └── Hypanthodium (Ficus)
conceptBreakdown.content: An inflorescence is the natural arrangement of a cluster of flowers on a specialized floral axis called the **Peduncle**.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 4.1 Racemose vs. Cymose Comparison Matrix
conceptBreakdown.title: 4.1 Racemose vs. Cymose Comparison Matrix
conceptBreakdown.content:
| Parameter | Racemose Inflorescence | Cymose Inflorescence |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Peduncle Growth** | **Indeterminate** (grows continuously via terminal vegetative/flowering apex) | **Determinate** (growth terminates in a flower) |
| **Floral Maturation Sequence** | **Acropetal** (older flowers at base, younger at apex) | **Basipetal** (older flower at center/apex, younger at base) |
| **Opening Order** | **Centripetal** (outer flowers open first toward center) | **Centrifugal** (inner/central flower opens first toward periphery) |
| **Major Variants** | Raceme (*Mustard*), Spike (*Achyranthes*), Spadix (*Colocasia*), Corymb (*Iberis*), Umbel (*Centella*), **Capitulum / Head** (*Sunflower*) | Monochasial / Uniparous Helicoid & Scorpioid (*Begonia*), Dichasial / Biparous (*Dianthus*), Polychasial / Multiparous (*Calotropis*) |

conceptBreakdown.heading: 4.2 Specialized Inflorescences
conceptBreakdown.title: 4.2 Specialized Inflorescences
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
SPECIALIZED INFLORESCENCES
                       
   1. CYATHIUM (*Euphorbia*)
      ├── Cup-shaped Involucre with nectar glands.
      ├── Single central, highly long-stalked FEMALE FLOWER (tricarpellary gynoecium).
      └── Surrounded by multiple scorpioid centrifugally arranged MALE FLOWERS
          (each reduced to a single stamen!).
          
   2. VERTICILLASTER (*Ocimum* / *Salvia* - Lamiaceae)
      ├── False whorl at nodes consisting of two condensed opposite dichasia 
          transitioning into scorpioid cymes.
          
   3. HYPANTHODIUM (*Ficus* - Fig / Banyan)
      ├── Fleshy globose receptacle forming a hollow cavity with an apical pore (**Ostiole**).
      └── Internal Flowers: Male near ostiole, Female at base, Sterile **Gall Flowers** in between.
conceptBreakdown.content:
1. **Cyathium (*Euphorbia*)**: Cup-shaped involucre with nectar glands enclosing a single long-stalked central female flower surrounded by multiple centrifugally arranged male flowers (each reduced to a single stamen).
2. **Verticillaster (*Ocimum*, *Salvia*)**: False whorls at stem nodes formed by condensed opposite dichasia transitioning into scorpioid cymes.
3. **Hypanthodium (*Ficus*)**: Fleshy pyriform/globose receptacle enclosing a hollow cavity with an apical ostiole housing male flowers (near ostiole), female flowers (at base), and sterile gall flowers (pollinated by *Blastophaga* wasps).
